title: Unveiling the Security Risks Driven by the Hardware Interrupts
evidence_span: The authors report an automated framework for discovering interrupt working features and trigger conditions, six vulnerable interrupts, attack primitives that leak secrets, and four demonstrations including restricted-directory leakage, DNN-architecture fingerprinting, process classification, and Spectre enhancement.
problem: Poorly managed hardware interrupts expose low-level events to unprivileged software and create unexpected attack surfaces.
method_or_artifact: Automated interrupt-feature and trigger-condition testing framework plus interrupt-based secret-leakage attack primitives.
workload_or_benchmark: Six discovered vulnerable interrupts and four attack demonstrations; systems, kernels, devices, and comparison coverage are unspecified.
hardware_or_process_assumptions: Computer systems with hardware interrupts observable or triggerable by unprivileged software; privilege boundaries, CPU, OS, and interrupt-controller details are unspecified.
baselines: Spectre attack without the proposed enhancement
limits: The description omits processor/OS configurations, exploit prerequisites, leakage rates, mitigations, and false-positive analysis.
Demonstrations establish attack feasibility but not prevalence across platforms or practical end-to-end exploit cost.
Official description only; security claims require paper-level and responsible-disclosure verification.

title: Leveraging AI-Inspired Hardware Architecture to Enhance LPN Acceleration in Post-Quantum Cryptography
evidence_span: LHPA is described as an FPGA LPN accelerator with heterogeneous configurable engines, stage-level scheduling, and a bandwidth-oriented performance model; the official description reports a 52.80x gain over the state-of-the-art LPN architecture.
problem: Existing LPN accelerators optimize isolated computation while overlooking execution flow and data-transfer bottlenecks in post-quantum cryptography.
method_or_artifact: AI-inspired heterogeneous FPGA architecture with configurable engines, stage-level scheduling, and bandwidth-oriented performance modeling for LPN.
workload_or_benchmark: LPN acceleration workloads on FPGAs; parameter sets, security level, FPGA family, clock, resource use, and state-of-the-art baseline are unspecified.
hardware_or_process_assumptions: FPGA-based post-quantum cryptography accelerator with heterogeneous engines and bandwidth-limited data movement; device and memory-interface details are unspecified.
metrics: 52.80x performance gain over the state-of-the-art LPN architecture
limits: The description omits LPN parameters, security assumptions, FPGA resource/clock results, energy, throughput definition, and baseline implementation details.
A large relative gain may depend on data-transfer bottlenecks or baseline maturity and does not establish cryptographic superiority.
Official description only; performance and security claims require paper-level verification.

title: UNCHARTED: A Universal Circuit Design Hierarchical Model Based on Auto-Regressive Spatio-Temporal Graph Neural Network with Exogenous Driving Inputs
evidence_span: UNCHARTED models transient behavior of circuit components with an auto-regressive spatio-temporal graph neural network, uses low-rank adaptation for sizing, and applies back-propagation for inverse design; the official description claims up to 241.9x simulation acceleration, over 95% SPICE similarity in more than 70% of tested circuits, and delay-chain/amplifier optimization examples.
problem: Analog circuit design and transient simulation are time-consuming and depend heavily on expert designers.
method_or_artifact: Hierarchical graph-neural surrogate for transient simulation with low-rank sizing adaptation and back-propagation-based inverse design.
workload_or_benchmark: Analog transient circuits including delay chains and amplifiers, compared with SPICE; circuit count, topology distribution, simulation settings, and training/test split are unspecified.
hardware_or_process_assumptions: Analog circuit component graphs and SPICE-like transient behavior; process technology, model cards, solver settings, and hardware used for inference are unspecified.
metrics: More than 95% similarity to SPICE in over 70% of tested circuits
Inverse-design demonstrations for a delay chain and an amplifier
limits: The description omits circuit dataset scale, process corners, accuracy distribution, failed cases, training cost, and solver/inference hardware.
Similarity above 95% for a subset does not establish robust yield, corner, or out-of-distribution behavior.
Official description only; surrogate fidelity and design-quality claims require paper-level verification.

title: Cache Where It Counts: Towards Workload-Aware I/O Coordination for NUMA Storage Systems
evidence_span: Laelaps combines storage-topology-aware page-cache placement, storage-topology-aware I/O-thread scheduling, and workload-aware adaptive eviction for distributed NVMe on NUMA servers; evaluation reports 1.41x geometric-mean throughput improvement with 3.5% runtime overhead.
problem: NUMA storage stacks ignore storage topology, cache locality, and workload-specific eviction, causing cross-node accesses and poor I/O coordination.
method_or_artifact: Workload-aware I/O coordination framework aligning page-cache placement and I/O-thread scheduling with NVMe topology and selecting eviction policies from observed access patterns.
workload_or_benchmark: NUMA servers with distributed NVMe storage and diverse application access patterns; workloads, devices, node counts, and baseline policies are unspecified.
hardware_or_process_assumptions: NUMA CPU/memory topology with distributed NVMe devices and an OS page-cache/I/O scheduling path; kernel, PCIe topology, CPU, and device details are unspecified.
baselines: conventional I/O scheduling and rigid page-cache eviction
programmable cache policies requiring manual tuning
limits: The description omits workload mix, tail latency, fairness, topology scale, policy-selection overhead, and per-workload variance.
Geometric-mean gains can conceal regressions and depend on the selected storage and NUMA configuration.
Official description only; systems results require paper-level trace and baseline verification.

title: Scalable Reliability Assessment of DNNs Through Simultaneous Fault Injection
evidence_span: The work identifies artificial masking from interacting simultaneous faults in densely connected DNNs, proposes interaction mitigation and pruning of non-critical inputs, and reports nearly 42 million SW/RTL injections with false negatives as low as 0% and average injection-time gains of 3.82x RTL and 5.29x SW.
problem: Conventional DNN fault injection does not scale to large models, while simultaneous injection can interact and create false negatives that misclassify critical faults.
method_or_artifact: Interaction-aware simultaneous fault-injection assessment with mitigation of artificial masking and input-batch pruning for further acceleration.
workload_or_benchmark: DNN fault campaigns at software and RTL abstraction levels totaling nearly 42 million injections; models, fault distributions, hardware, and baseline tool details are unspecified.
hardware_or_process_assumptions: DNN implementations evaluated at SW and RTL levels with transient-fault injection; target accelerator/processor, RTL design, and fault model are unspecified.
metrics: False negatives as low as 0%, average 0.2%
limits: The description omits model architectures, fault distributions, accuracy criteria, campaign cost, and per-model variance.
Low false-negative rates may depend on the interaction model and selected pruning threshold; other fault classes may behave differently.
Official description only; reliability conclusions require paper-level campaign and oracle verification.
